title: Marked flat algebra lifts, their classes and cotangent localization equation
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. A base datum consists of finite-dimensional $k$-algebras $C',C$ [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace], with local residue-marked structures in the sense of [def-sfb-artin-deformation-test-category] specialized to $R=k$, and a surjective augmentation-preserving $k$-algebra map $q:C'\to C$ such that $\mathfrak m_{C'}\ker(q)=0$. No nonzero or one-dimensional-kernel condition is imposed. Put $I=\ker(q)$ with its inherited $k$-module structure. For a $C$-algebra $B$, define $P=k\otimes_C B$ and $N=P\otimes_k I$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. A marked flat lift is a commutative algebra $E$ over $C'$ with flat structure map [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and a surjective reduction map $r:E\to B$ satisfying $r\circ s=(C\to B)\circ q$ and $\ker(r)=I E$. Equivalently this reduction specifies a $C$-algebra isomorphism $C\otimes_{C'}E\cong B$. Two lifts are isomorphic if a $C'$-algebra isomorphism between them commutes with the reduction maps; let $\mathrm{Classes}(B)$ be the quotient by these isomorphisms. For the full standard cotangent complex [def-trf-cotangent-resolution-data], define $T^j(B)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(P)}(L_{P/k},N[ j ])$ with $N$ in degree zero and ordinary module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; addition is addition of derived morphisms. For a $C$-algebra map $f:B\to U$, the coefficient map is $p\otimes i\mapsto f_P(p)\otimes i$. A pair $t\in T^j(B)$, $v\in T^j(U)$ satisfies the cotangent localization equation when restriction of $v$ precomposed with the standard cotangent map equals $t$ postcomposed with this coefficient map, using the exact-restriction shift and degree-zero comparisons. For $S\subset P$ multiplicative, a lift of $U$ is a localization of a lift of $B$ if its thick-base map and reduction square commute and its algebra is the localization at the inverse image of $S$ under $E\to B\to P$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization].
